---
title: "Joining tables: left, inner, full and anti (solutions)"
format: html
---

Teacher version. Chunks run. The tables come with the dplyr package, so no data file is needed.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(tidyverse)
```

## Look at the tables

```{r}
#| label: look-members
band_members
```

```{r}
#| label: look-instruments
band_instruments
```

Answer: both tables share `name`. John and Paul appear in both tables.

## Your turn 1: left_join()

```{r}
#| label: turn-1
band_members |>
  left_join(band_instruments, join_by(name))
```

Answer: 3 rows. Mick has `NA` in `plays` because `band_instruments` has no row for him.

## Your turn 2: swap the tables

```{r}
#| label: turn-2
band_instruments |>
  left_join(band_members, join_by(name))
```

Answer: 3 rows. Keith has `NA` in `band`. `left_join()` keeps all rows of the left table, so the table order changes the result.

## Your turn 3: inner_join()

```{r}
#| label: turn-3
band_members |>
  inner_join(band_instruments, join_by(name))
```

Answer: 2 rows, John and Paul. Mick and Keith are missing because each appears in only one table.

## Your turn 4: full_join()

```{r}
#| label: turn-4
band_members |>
  full_join(band_instruments, join_by(name))
```

Answer: 4 rows. Mick has no `plays` and Keith has no `band`.

## Your turn 5: anti_join()

```{r}
#| label: turn-5
band_members |>
  anti_join(band_instruments, join_by(name))
```

Answer: Mick, 1 row. The result has only the columns of `band_members`.

## Your turn 6: choose the join

| Question | Join |
|----------|------|
| All members of the band, with or without an instrument | `left_join()` |
| Only people with a band and an instrument | `inner_join()` |
| All four people, whatever is missing | `full_join()` |
| Members with no instrument | `anti_join()` |

## Notes for the teacher

- The slide "Name the key" runs `left_join()` without `join_by()`. dplyr prints `Joining with by = join_by(name)`. The result is the same, and the key stays implicit.
- The slides show `anti_join(band_instruments, band_members)` as the example (Keith). Your turn 5 reverses the tables (Mick).
- `anti_join()` returns later in the course to find countries that do not match between two tables.
- If time runs short, Your turn 6 becomes homework.
